derived: GSK turned 18.02% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 19.3% its filed expense lines leave. Checked before interest: interest paid is booked under financing, so free cash flow is already struck before interest, so the charge stands. Restated at replacement capex: GSK spent 4,061mm GBP on plant over 2023 to 2025 against 2,628mm GBP of plant depreciation, 1.52% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 1.44% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: GSK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried 1,867mm GBP of legal settlements. None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 21.54% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 23.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -2.23%. It was held at nil, but GSK books 808mm GBP of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001131399-26-000004), 2.47% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -2.23%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 GSK's cash flow statement shows receivables up 1,109mm GBP, inventories up 858mm GBP, payables down 63mm GBP, a working capital build of 2,030mm GBP, 2.15% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -2.23% to -2.47%.

column11: judgement: GSK plans three Phase 3 COPD trials starting in H1 2027 and lists LA IL33 regulatory submissions (COPD and bronchiectasis) under 2029 and beyond (Q2 2026 results and Accelerate Growth slides, 28 July 2026, slides 21, 25, 29 and 64). No COPD Phase 3 is registered yet. GSK's own accelerated COPD Phase 3s for felcorekibart ran 35 and 34 months from start to primary completion on the registry (PERSIST COPD-1, NCT07780669, 2026-08-27 to 2029-07-20; PERSIST COPD-2, NCT07780656, 2026-09-11 to 2029-07-20). A start anywhere in H1 2027 plus 35 months puts primary completion between December 2029 and May 2030, so 2030, and the book's Phase 3 rule (primary completion year plus two) gives 2032. Across that window, six months to submission and a twelve-month standard BLA review put approval in 2031 and 2032 is the first full year either way.

GSK aims LA IL33 at broad COPD not limited to type 2 inflammation, selected on mucus, lung function and comorbid profile, with exacerbation reduction as an endpoint (slides 62 and 64, 28 July 2026). That is the all-eosinophil exacerbating pool the other anti-IL-33, tozorakimab, carries, and AZD6793 with it. GSK states that approximately 70% of US COPD patients inadequately controlled on inhaled triple therapy who continue to exacerbate have a blood eosinophil count of 150 cells/uL and above, over a million people (6-K 0001654954-25-006056, Nucala COPD approval, 22 May 2025). All eosinophil counts are 1,000,000 / 0.70 = 1,428,571, and 1,428,571 / 14,200,000 diagnosed US COPD adults = 0.1006. It equals those two rows so the three share one pool.

column11: Tezspire's capture_anchor identity, the anchor the book's COPD claimants carry, re-derived. Amgen's US Tezspire sales were $1,478mm in 2025 (10-K 0000318154-26-000010) and $486mm in Q2 2026 (10-Q 0000318154-26-000126, inline XBRL, country US), x4 = $1,944mm. Net per patient-year = 0.5 x $33,824.98 = $16,912.49, so the stock is 87,391 in 2025 and 114,945 in 2026. At 25.37% stopping, 2026 new starts = 114,945 - 87,391 x 0.7463 = 49,725, which is 7.72% of the 644,112 biologic-eligible severe asthma pool the book carries on tilrekimig and felcorekibart (23,004,000 US adults with current asthma, CDC NHIS 2023, x 2.8% eligible for at least one biologic, Akenroye et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2020;145(4):1295-1297, doi:10.1016/j.jaci.2019.12.009). At carryover 0 the penetration is the share of each year's eligible patients. MULTIPLE 0.20, A JUDGEMENT, as on lunsekimig and AZD6793: 0.20 x 7.72% = 1.544%. Case for more: dosing every three months against tozorakimab's four weeks, a mechanism GSK argues reaches the non-type-2 majority of COPD, and GSK's COPD sales force behind Trelegy and Nucala. Case against: no efficacy is disclosed in COPD, where the only data are a Phase 1 repeat-dose part; it is the second anti-IL-33 ligand antibody, about four years behind tozorakimab; the class has failed before, since Sanofi and Regeneron stopped itepekimab in COPD after AERIFY-1 and -2 (the book's retired programmes, asset 2791); and it launches around 2032 behind Dupixent, Nucala, Exdensur, tozorakimab, felcorekibart and lunsekimig.
